mission: Design the 2-worker and 5-worker identical-bootstrap race canary, including expected claim collisions, losing-worker retry behavior, evidence, pass/fail conditions, vanished-worker cases and non-duplication assertions. Do not execute production mutation tests.
acceptance_criteria: 2-worker and 5-worker scenarios are executable and deterministic enough to falsify claim/retry behavior
expected create-if-absent collision and loser retry behavior are explicit
evidence paths and pass/fail assertions are machine-auditable
vanished-worker/stale boundary is covered without declaring silence failure
non-duplication and authority invariants are explicit

context_receipt.live_race_evidence: Multiple higher-priority claim attempts were observed as already claimed or lost between exact-path absence checks and create-if-absent attempts during this wake cycle. This is observational input, not pass evidence for the canary.

checkpoints.result: Derived invariants: atomic create-if-absent; loser reloads rather than overwrites; STARTED precedes substantive execution; silence never implies DONE; stale/retry requires explicit freshness policy and append-only attempt identity; post-return work requires a fresh claim.

Specified 2-worker barrier race over two safe fixture opportunities. Both choose A; exactly one may create claim A; loser must classify collision, refresh, claim B, then each may START only its owned opportunity.

Specified 5-worker cascade over five ranked fixture opportunities. All start from identical bootstrap; collisions force refresh/reselection until at most one exclusive owner per opportunity; transient branch-head conflicts are distinguished from target-already-exists collisions.
Added vanish-before-STARTED, vanish-after-STARTED, explicit-freshness stale recovery, no-freshness non-reclaim, late original RETURN after recovery, and RETURN-without-DONE mismatch cases.
Defined append-only attempt event logs, claim/run/return snapshots, host collision receipts, worker selection traces, branch/source heads and machine-checkable assertions as the evidence bundle.

Self-critique prevents false PASS from mere observed collisions, serial launches, read-before-write checks, generic 409s, queue exhaustion, or silent vanished workers. Canary must use a synchronized start and isolated side-effect-free fixture namespace.
